title: Romans Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Romans 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I say the truth in Christ
For I could wish that myself were accursed
For this is the word of promise
questions.correctAnswer: I say the truth in Christ
questions.explanation: The phrase 'I say the truth in Christ' is the very first statement made in Romans 9:1.

questions.question: What does Paul express about his feelings in Romans 9?
options: He has joy in his heart
He has great heaviness and continual sorrow
He is happy for the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: He has great heaviness and continual sorrow
questions.explanation: Romans 9:2 states that Paul has 'great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart'.

questions.question: For whom does Paul wish to be accursed according to Romans 9?
options: His kinsmen according to the flesh
questions.correctAnswer: His kinsmen according to the flesh
questions.explanation: In Romans 9:3, Paul expresses that he could wish he were accursed for 'my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh'.

questions.question: What is stated about the Israelites in Romans 9:4?
options: They are not God's chosen people
They have the adoption and covenants
questions.correctAnswer: They have the adoption and covenants
questions.explanation: Romans 9:4 states that to the Israelites pertain 'the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants'.

questions.question: Who came from the Israelites according to Romans 9:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 9:5 mentions that Christ came from the Israelites, stating 'of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came'.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:6 clarify about Israel?
options: All who are of Israel are God's people
Israel is only a physical nation
questions.correctAnswer: Not all Israel is Israel
questions.explanation: Romans 9:6 states 'For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel', indicating a distinction.

questions.question: According to Romans 9:7, who are considered children?
options: In Isaac shall thy seed be called
questions.correctAnswer: In Isaac shall thy seed be called
questions.explanation: Romans 9:7 states 'but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called', indicating who is considered children.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:8 say about the children of the flesh?
options: They are all children of God
They are not the children of God
questions.correctAnswer: They are not the children of God
questions.explanation: Romans 9:8 states 'They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God'.

questions.question: What is the promise mentioned in Romans 9:9?
options: At this time will I come, and Isaac shall have a son
At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son
At this time will I come, and Jacob shall have a son
At this time will I come, and Rebecca shall have a son
questions.correctAnswer: At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son
questions.explanation: Romans 9:9 states, 'this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son'.

questions.question: Who conceived by Isaac according to Romans 9:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Rebecca
questions.explanation: Romans 9:10 mentions 'when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac'.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:11 say about the children being not yet born?
options: They had done good or evil
They were to inherit the kingdom
The purpose of God according to election might stand
questions.correctAnswer: The purpose of God according to election might stand
questions.explanation: Romans 9:11 states 'that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth'.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul experiences sorrow in his heart according to Romans 9?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Romans 9:2 indicates that Paul has 'great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart'.

questions.question: Is it true that Christ came according to the flesh from the Israelites?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Romans 9:5 states 'of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came', affirming that Christ came from the Israelites.

questions.question: Is it true that all children of the flesh are children of God according to Romans 9?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 9:8 states 'the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God', indicating that not all children of the flesh are children of God.

questions.question: Is it true that the promise mentioned in Romans 9:9 refers to Rebecca having a son?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 9:9 states the promise is about Sarah having a son, not Rebecca.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was said unto Rebecca regarding her sons?
options: The elder shall serve the younger.
The younger shall serve the elder.
questions.correctAnswer: The elder shall serve the younger.
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Romans 9:12, which quotes God's declaration about the roles of Jacob and Esau.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:16 indicate will happen if one relies on their own will or efforts?
options: It is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: It is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:16 emphasizes that mercy is determined by God, not by human effort or desire.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:13 say about God's feelings towards Jacob and Esau?
options: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
Esau have I loved, but Jacob have I hated.
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:13 explicitly states God's love for Jacob and His rejection of Esau.

questions.question: What is the purpose of God raising Pharaoh according to Romans 9:17?
options: To show His power and declare His name.
questions.correctAnswer: To show His power and declare His name.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:17 describes God's intention in raising Pharaoh to demonstrate His power and make His name known.

questions.question: According to Romans 9:14, is there unrighteousness with God?
questions.correctAnswer: No, God forbid.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:14 affirms that there is no unrighteousness with God, emphasizing His just nature.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:18 teach about God's mercy?
options: God has mercy on whom He will have mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: God has mercy on whom He will have mercy.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:18 asserts that God's mercy is selective and according to His will.

questions.question: What question does Romans 9:19 raise concerning God's will?
options: Why doth He yet find fault?
How can we understand His ways?
questions.correctAnswer: Why doth He yet find fault?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:19 poses the question of how God can find fault with humanity if no one can resist His will.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:20 imply about humanity's role in questioning God?
questions.correctAnswer: Humans should not question God.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:20 emphasizes that humanity does not have the authority to question the Creator's decisions.

questions.question: What analogy does Romans 9:21 use to explain God's sovereignty?
questions.correctAnswer: A potter and the clay.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:21 uses the analogy of a potter having power over clay to illustrate God's authority over creation.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:22 suggest about God's patience?
questions.correctAnswer: God endures with much longsuffering.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:22 indicates that God shows great patience even towards those destined for destruction.

questions.question: What is the significance of the promise mentioned in Romans 9:9?
options: Sarah will have a son at this time.
Both Jacob and Esau will be favored.
questions.correctAnswer: Sarah will have a son at this time.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:9 highlights the specific promise made regarding the birth of Isaac's son, affirming God's faithfulness.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:11 say about God's purpose related to election?
options: It stands not of works but of him that calleth.
It is based on human effort.
questions.correctAnswer: It stands not of works but of him that calleth.
questions.explanation: Romans 9:11 clarifies that God's election is based on His calling, not on human actions.

questions.question: Is it true that God shows mercy to everyone equally?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 9:18 indicates that God has mercy on whom He chooses, suggesting it is not given equally to all.

questions.question: Is it true that humanity can resist God's will?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Romans 9:19, it questions who can resist God's will, implying that it is ultimately unresistible.

questions.question: Is it true that God has no control over the fate of individuals?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Romans 9:21 illustrates that God has the power to shape individuals as He pleases, thus demonstrating His control over fate.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 9.

questions.question: What does God intend to make known through the vessels of mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: The riches of his glory
questions.explanation: This is stated in Romans 9:23, where it says that God might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy.

questions.question: Who are the 'vessels of mercy' mentioned in Romans 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Both Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 9:24 specifies that God has called us, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles, indicating both groups are included.

questions.question: According to Romans 9:26, who will be called the children of the living God?
options: Those who are part of Israel
Those who are not my people
questions.correctAnswer: Those who are not my people
questions.explanation: Romans 9:26 states that in the place where it was said unto them, 'Ye are not my people,' there shall they be called the children of the living God.

questions.question: What does Romans 9:30 say about the Gentiles?
options: They have followed after the law
questions.correctAnswer: They have attained to righteousness
questions.explanation: Romans 9:30 concludes that the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness through faith.

questions.question: What caused Israel to stumble according to Romans 9:32?
options: Their failure to follow the law
Their reliance on works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Their reliance on works of the law
questions.explanation: Romans 9:32 explains that Israel sought righteousness not by faith but by the works of the law, causing them to stumble.

questions.question: What is the 'stumblingstone' mentioned in Romans 9:33?
questions.correctAnswer: A rock of offense
questions.explanation: Romans 9:33 refers to the stumblingstone and rock of offense, emphasizing that whosoever believes on him shall not be ashamed.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'oikonomia' in Romans 9:24 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Stewardship
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'oikonomia' means stewardship, reflecting God's management of salvation for both Jews and Gentiles.

questions.question: What literary technique is used in Romans 9:27, where it mentions a remnant shall be saved?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The mention of a remnant in Romans 9:27 foreshadows the future salvation of a select group of Israel, emphasizing God's mercy.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Romans 9:24's theme of calling from the Gentiles?
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 3:28
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:28 echoes the theme that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Gentile, emphasizing the inclusive calling from God.

questions.question: Which other passage fulfills the promise mentioned in Romans 9:26 about being called children of God?
questions.correctAnswer: John 1:12
questions.explanation: John 1:12 states that as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, fulfilling the promise in Romans 9:26.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Romans 9:30?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 9:29
questions.explanation: Romans 9:29 discusses the remnant that God preserved, leading into the discussion of the Gentiles in Romans 9:30.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'vessels of wrath' in Romans 9:22?
questions.correctAnswer: They represent judgment
questions.explanation: The 'vessels of wrath' in Romans 9:22 symbolize those who are destined for judgment, contrasting with the vessels of mercy.

questions.question: The concept of 'election' mentioned in Romans 9 implies what about God's choice?
options: It is based on human effort
It is according to God's purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It is according to God's purpose
questions.explanation: Romans 9:11 highlights that the purpose of God according to election stands, emphasizing divine sovereignty in His choices.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 9 indicates that all Israel will be saved.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The chapter indicates that only a remnant will be saved, as stated in Romans 9:27.

questions.question: True or False: Esaias prophesied about the calling of the Gentiles.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in Romans 9:25, where Paul quotes Esaias regarding calling those who were not my people.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 9:6 teach about the relationship between ethnic Israel and the true people of God?
options: Not all who are descended from Israel are true Israel
All Israelites are guaranteed salvation by birthright
The law alone determines who belongs to Israel
Ethnic descent is the sole basis for God's promises
questions.correctAnswer: Not all who are descended from Israel are true Israel
questions.explanation: Romans 9:6 states that "they are not all Israel, which are of Israel," indicating that ethnic descent does not guarantee membership in the true people of God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 9:11 teach concerning God's election?
options: God's election is based on His sovereign purpose, not human works
Election is determined by human merit and good deeds
God chooses based on the moral performance of individuals
Election depends on the firstborn status of the individual
questions.correctAnswer: God's election is based on His sovereign purpose, not human works
questions.explanation: Romans 9:11 explains that God's purpose of election stands "not of works, but of him that calleth," emphasizing election is God's sovereign choice, not human effort.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine mercy does Romans 9:15 teach?
options: God shows mercy according to His own sovereign will
God's mercy is deserved by human effort
Mercy is equally distributed to all people
Mercy is given only to the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy according to His own sovereign will
questions.explanation: Romans 9:15 quotes God saying, 'I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy,' showing that mercy is granted according to God's sovereign decision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 9:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Romans 9:18 states that God 'hath mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth,' highlighting God's absolute sovereignty over mercy and judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 9:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Romans 9:22 speaks of God enduring 'with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction,' showing His patient endurance before executing judgment.

questions.question: How does Romans 9:7 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant promise fulfillment?
options: It highlights that the covenant promise is fulfilled through Isaac, not merely physical descent
It teaches that all descendants of Abraham are automatically heirs of the promise
It denies any future significance to Abraham’s seed
It emphasizes that the law is the basis for covenant inclusion
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights that the covenant promise is fulfilled through Isaac, not merely physical descent
questions.explanation: Romans 9:7 states, 'In Isaac shall thy seed be called,' emphasizing the covenant promise is based on the promise to Isaac rather than just physical descent from Abraham.

questions.question: How does Romans 9:24 relate to the inclusion of Gentiles in God's redemptive plan?
options: It teaches that God calls both Jews and Gentiles to be vessels of mercy
It restricts God's calling only to ethnic Jews
It states Gentiles are excluded from God's promises
It emphasizes works as the basis for Gentile inclusion
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God calls both Jews and Gentiles to be vessels of mercy
questions.explanation: Romans 9:24 states God calls 'not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles,' indicating Gentiles are included in God's mercy and redemptive plan.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 9:13 and Romans 9:15 teach about God's election and mercy?
options: God's election and mercy are based on His sovereign will, independent of human merit
Election is based on human works and deservingness
God loves all equally without distinction
Mercy is given randomly without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God's election and mercy are based on His sovereign will, independent of human merit
questions.explanation: Romans 9:13 quotes God loving Jacob and hating Esau, and 9:15 states He shows mercy on whom He wills, together affirming election and mercy as sovereign acts of God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 9:20 and Romans 9:21 teach about human response to divine sovereignty?
options: Humans have no standing to question God's sovereign purposes
Humans can demand explanations from God about His actions
God’s sovereignty is limited by human free will
God must justify His actions to human reasoning
questions.correctAnswer: Humans have no standing to question God's sovereign purposes
questions.explanation: Romans 9:20-21 teach that man, the creature, should not question the Creator's sovereign decisions, using the analogy of the potter and clay to illustrate God's authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 9:30 and Romans 9:31 teach about righteousness and faith?
options: Righteousness is attained by faith, not by works of the law
Righteousness comes only through adherence to the law
All who follow the law attain righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness is attained by faith, not by works of the law
questions.explanation: Romans 9:30-31 contrasts Gentiles attaining righteousness by faith with Israel failing because they sought it by works of the law, teaching justification by faith alone.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 9:32 and Romans 9:33 teach about the stumbling stone and Israel’s failure?
options: Israel stumbled at Christ, the appointed stumbling stone, because they sought righteousness by works
Israel fully embraced Christ as the foundation
The law was sufficient for Israel's righteousness
The stumbling stone refers to the law itself
questions.correctAnswer: Israel stumbled at Christ, the appointed stumbling stone, because they sought righteousness by works
questions.explanation: Romans 9:32-33 states Israel stumbled at the 'stumblingstone' because they sought righteousness by works, while faith in Christ prevents shame.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Romans 9:19-21 teaches that God’s sovereignty removes human responsibility. What does Romans 9:19-21 actually teach?
options: Humans should not question God's sovereign decisions but are still accountable
Humans have no responsibility because God controls all
God forces people to sin without their consent
Human free will overrides God's sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Humans should not question God's sovereign decisions but are still accountable
questions.explanation: Romans 9:19-21 rebukes questioning God's sovereignty but does not deny human responsibility; it emphasizes God's authority in creation and judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 9:2 teach about the apostolic experience of intercession and sorrow for the lost?
options: Paul experiences deep sorrow and heaviness for the salvation of his brethren
The apostle is indifferent to the lost
Sorrow is unnecessary because all are saved
questions.correctAnswer: Paul experiences deep sorrow and heaviness for the salvation of his brethren
questions.explanation: Romans 9:2 states Paul has 'great heaviness and continual sorrow' in his heart for his kinsmen, showing the apostolic burden for Israel's salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 9:23 specifically demonstrate in relation to God's purpose for mercy?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: Romans 9:23 says God 'might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy,' demonstrating the divine attribute of glory especially in mercy.

questions.question: How does Romans 9:27 connect to the broader theological theme of election and remnant in Israel?
options: Though Israel is numerous, only a remnant will be saved by grace
All Israel will ultimately be saved without exception
The remnant concept denies God's sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Though Israel is numerous, only a remnant will be saved by grace
questions.explanation: Romans 9:27 quotes Isaiah to affirm that despite Israel's vast numbers, only a remnant will be saved, highlighting the doctrine of election and grace.
